interactive.title: Solve √(x + 2) = x and Reject Extraneous Root
interactive.instructions: Square both sides (noting this is a one-way implication requiring x >= 0), solve the resulting quadratic, and explicitly reject any extraneous root.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Solve square root of x plus 2 equals x step by step
interactive.fallbackText: Square both sides as a one-way implication, solve the quadratic, and substitute candidates back into the original radical equation.
hints: Squaring both sides gives x + 2 = x^2, which may introduce an extraneous root.
Check both candidates in sqrt(x + 2) = x.

sharedIndependentMarks.description: Explicitly reject extraneous candidate x = -1 after checking original equation

marks.description: Square both sides (one-way implication) to obtain x^2 - x - 2 = 0

steps.note: Square both sides — one-way implication (valid when x >= 0; must check candidates in original equation).
Candidate solutions from the squared equation.
Test in √(x + 2) = x: x = 2 gives √4 = 2 (valid); x = -1 gives √1 = 1 ≠ -1 (extraneous, rejected).

interactive.title: Double-Angle Identity: sin(2x)
interactive.instructions: Write the double-angle form 2*sin(x)*cos(x). Because double-angle trig identities lie outside bounded symbolic rules, the verifier reports Indeterminate rather than falsely marking your step wrong.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Double-angle trigonometric identity workspace
interactive.fallbackText: Recall the double-angle identity for sin(2x) and compare with the worked solution.

steps.note: Standard double-angle identity (outside bounded symbolic proof rules, so reported transparently as indeterminate during step check).
